title: Investigate asymmetric token attribution during cross-cluster failover with retransmit suppression
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer escalations report unexplained monthly credit variance after regional cluster failover. Symptoms: a subset of streaming sessions in Hosted and Dedicated modes show asymmetric token attribution (some downstream shards attribute tokens but upstream ledger shows fewer tokens), leading to under-billing for some customers and negative invoice adjustments when reconciled. Investigation points to retransmit suppression logic in the proxy layer during cross-cluster handoff causing idempotency metadata to be dropped for retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create long-lived streaming session (streaming chat) on region A that triggers periodic prefetch/prefix caching.
2) Simulate regional failover by draining and failing over to region B proxy (failover orchestrator test harness).
3) Force a subset of inflight token batches to be retransmitted with proxy-level suppression enabled (internal flag).
4) Observe ledger and tenant usage aggregation; compare per-request attribution headers with final billing ledger entries and replay logs.
investigation_notes: - Correlated customer reports from three tenants; all on hybrid routing (hosted->dedicated fallback) using streaming and prefetch enabled.
- Proxy logs show retransmit suppression metric 'retransmit_suppressed=true' for ~0.7% of inflight batches around failover window.
- Downstream shards accepted and counted tokens; upstream metering emitter failed to include idempotency token header after suppression, causing ledger ingestion to dedupe and drop the events.
- Reproduction in staging when enabling suppression flag; disabling suppression removes discrepancy.
- Edge case identified: suppression path strips X-Idempotency and X-Session-Seq when proxy reconnects to new cluster manager and falls back to zero-copy replay path.
root_cause: A race between the proxy retransmit-suppression optimization and the idempotency header propagation during cross-cluster failover. When retransmit suppression is active, the proxy returns a short-circuit ack to the client and suppresses remote retry metadata. During cluster handoff the suppressed path lost X-Idempotency headers resulting in ledger ingestion treating tokens as duplicates and dropping them.
proposed_fix: 1) Patch proxy to preserve idempotency and session-sequence headers even when retransmit suppression is active. 2) Add defensive replication: attach a hashed event-sig to each token-batch payload consumed by the ledger so downstream counting is not solely reliant on headers. 3) Backfill affected windows by replaying suppressed batches from proxy debug logs and marking them as manual ingest items for billing reconcile.
rollout_plan: - Patch in proxy repo (PR ready) and run unit + integration tests in staging with failover harness.
- Canary deploy to a small subset of hosts in staging then to low-traffic region in production with runtime flag OFF by default.
- Enable runtime flag ON for canary hosts and watch metrics for incorrect double-counts for 24 hours.
- Gradually roll out to remaining hosts, monitor billing diffs, and enable automated backfill job after verification.
- Communicate to ops and billing: planned maintenance window for backfill and potential invoice adjustments.
tests: - Unit tests for header-preservation code paths.
- Integration test with failover harness that asserts ledger count equals downstream shard count under retransmit conditions.
- Chaos test: simulate partial network partitions and ensure idempotency headers survive reconnection.
- End-to-end billing reconciliation test that runs a synthetic tenant through failover and verifies no negative invoice deltas.
monitoring: - Dashboard: per-tenant token attribution delta (downstream_count - ledger_count) over rolling 1h/24h windows.
